name: Induced failure required
claim_class: Robustness, safety, and correctness claims: a report that says something is handled, isolated, recovered, prevented, rejected, or validated.
proof_obligation: The evidence must show two things together: the specific failure was actually made to happen, and the handling in question fired in response. A run that only exercises the happy path is not evidence for a failure-path claim. The check itself must assert a user-observable outcome, for example a real output file appearing, a rejected item missing from a queue, or a recovered job completing, and never an internal value the code trivially satisfies, such as a status column or a returned Ok. Ask whether the check would still pass if the feature produced nothing; if so, it is checking the wrong thing. This obligation applies to robustness, safety, and correctness claims, not to every sentence in a report. A hook checks mechanically that a robustness verb never appears without an evidence block naming the failure that was induced. Whether the check asserts an outcome a user could see, instead of an internal value the code satisfies for free, is a judgement a reviewer makes.
failure_mode: A claim of the form "X works" gets reported as validated when no executed path actually exercised X. Because the happy-path run and the claim share the same code, a green run looks like proof, but the code running without an error is not the same thing as the property holding.
origin_incident: No single recorded event is documented for this rule. It generalizes a recurring pattern seen across AI coding agent reports instead: an agent reports that an error path is handled based on a clean run that never triggers the error, so the report and the untested code both look fine from the outside.
